There are 2 things I noticed about Meursault, 1: he is hyper oberservant I mean he was able to detect and witness meany things in his surroundings ever so clearly and preciesly that you start to notice how detailed his discription are. 2nd He never devlops on how people impac his life. My theory is: Facing such large sizes of inputs Meursault had to shutdown his emotions to keep living. The missconception about Meursqult is that he feels nothing. Quite the opposit Meursault is so sensitive if it were to be scaled to our terms he would be over reacting. I know I look I am just BSing here but bear with me can you? Meursqult explicitly says he does not love Marie. However, we see him longing for herm wishing to meet her and stay with her.
Meursault fails our standards in 1 thing: REBELLION. He never rebelled against any thing "ca m'etegale" even when Ryhmond dragged him into his Drama he let himself be. The narrator (same person as Meursault) does not acknowledge his feelings because he can't see them not cuz they don't exist.
What happens here is that Meursault tuned himself to the big events like death disputes and everything, if they will happen eventually why rebel at all? It's the natural order of things. I have a theory on why but bare with me now, I can see 2 sides of Meursault; one that doesn't flinch even at his death row and one that the heat of the summer sun makes him irrational. These 2 don't exit seperatly they are effectivly the same person. They argument may be weird but I think it's like a filter where when he's unsensitive to the big things he becomes sensitive to the little things and vice versa.
So Meursult himself mentions how when he was younger he had dreams and ambitions before he started working. One thing that attracted my attention was the narrator's boss. The work place does not care about th person all it cares about is what a person can provide while we can live that hell where the human ability to provide is the sole thing that matters in Metamorphosis by Kafka, Albet Camus managed to paint a picture that shows what type of human we will become under that type of enviorement. My proof for this is where Meursault appologiezes to his boss for the death of his mother. The worse thing is the fact that his boss didn't care and zas in fact still mad about it.

I would like to mention (I don't know if I did it already) That Meursault's work condition seems to be the source of his "ca m'etegale" mentality. My theory is that his boss doesn't care about anything in his employees life so as a result that idea was planted in Meursault's subconcious mind that nothing his life does really matter, NOT EVEN HIS MOTHER. To survive his workspace he had to adapt by rejecting rebellion cuz that will against his favor.
Side note: He observes everything but analyses nothing.

title: Animal Farm
author: George Orwell
Comments:
Read in 01/2026
This book is a true genius in seeing and demonstrating the cycle of power. Orwell here had a near perfect excution of plot and thesis. We see the transition almost live it. The allagory works very well. though Historically Orwell was refering to the USSR, the story applies to many diffrent countries and totalitarian regimes. My favorite character: Boxer, plays a huge role in the argument. Altough I condemn him for his lack of doubt, in a way I cannot blame him for that. As we see most of the animals are uneducated and some are unable to be. And that's something snowball was rooting for. However, Boxer's flaw starts when he set the axiom that Napolian is always right. Boxer's tragedy starts to surface slowly as Napolian shifts more and more to the totalirian regim.
Since Boxer resembles the working class this allegory fits perfectly. Especially the ending where once Boxer was unable to provide any longer he was quickly disposed of just like an old rag that's too dirty to be washed. I liked the character of Binjamin as well, in a way I can relate to him: Though I may be projecting what I want to be I like how Benjamin was always able to see the bigger picture no matter what. Since day one when Napolian kicked Snowball, Benjamin knew that this will end similarly to what Jhonson was doing.
Another point worth mentioning is Squealer: This character is underrated. Napolian isn't as smart as he seems. But he knows where to sit and whom to put where; that's his strength. However, Squealer knows how to handle each and everyone with words making him a scary power.
That led to my conclusion that Napolian knew which force to use and when : His dogs worked on smart and weak animals like the pigs who were with snowball before the exile. On the other hand, Dumb and Strong won't lean in as easily to brute force which we see when dogs tried to attack Boxer he was too strong for them and that's where Squealer comes in. if you think about most are weak and dumb (wd), some are Strong and dumb(Sd), few are Smart and weak (wS), rarely There are those who are Strong and Smart (SS).
wd: follow easily
Sd: use Squaler
wS: use Dogs
SS: will be lonely
In fact, the only character that fits the SS category is Benjamin. Benjamin was smart enough to see what's going on and strng enough to act however he knew he was alone in his consiousness and that led him to be slightly depressive as a character.

title: The Trial
author: Franz Kafka
Comments:

I have mixed feelings about this one. In a way I like the premise the story and the plot, on the other way I Joseph K. taps on my nerves, it could be me but it annoyed me very much he was flirting left and right with every women he meets. Other than that the concept is very intressting.
I enjoyed How spoke of the power and regime and how buraucracy feels like an endless maze.
The converation with the painter actually changed how I was reading the book, I started seeing the projections more clearly. Joseph was a normal human living his own life. As the trial went on we see the policeman who ask for bribes, the corrupted jury, the harasser scholar, so on so forth. The painter did a zoom in on whzt was happening. Every time J.K. was trying to win his trial it felt like a loop a certain person suggests a solution to kafka's peoblem but every solution is basically a Qubit you just do it an hope for the best. Like the painter suggested pulling his strings but his strings only pulled the weak judges who should be linked to bigger judges who in their turn have suppevisors who are related to the people making the final descison. The painter discribes how no decision is truly final and the court can resume any proceedings even years after the decision has been made. Which felt weird, we hear about the higher ups but we never see them. The power is subdevised in the system so much that all the people that J.K has acess too can't do that much, only they could try to wiggle the proceedings to his favor. Add to that, everytime we see a person with relation to the court speak or explain somthing is basically a wave of hard Jargon that boils down to we got a handfull of coins we can toss if they land as we want it we get good result and we proceed to toss another coin else we get bad things and we have to try tossing a diffrent coin. This made J.K. burned down as he was slowly grinding against the system. That's exactly what the system was doing. In theory the court was build to garentee Justice and equity by pulling everyone into the same process regardless to who they are dividing power between a lot of people judges, juries, scholars to elimnate any bias. In practice, what happens is a diffrent story. As we follow Joseph, I notice something. People aren't there because work must be done but work is created from thin air to give people work to do. I notice this from the 1st hearing of J.K. that there were too many people there too many fo hearin, too many for the small room almost as if they were simply cuz they need to be there not to serve any purpose. So people are given enough power to feed their illusion but not to actually give them any real power to do anything that's why J.K. to cheat the system failed every time. What I find most intresting is how the people who hold some power are discribed as they hold absolute power which shouldn't be possible to ensure fairness. However, if we look at the system whoever is above basically controls you so the higher you are the more power you have and by projection we understand thatthe people who are at the top are the ones who own the staircase. Although this isn't directly mentioned it's not a streched conclusion. If we look at the workers they all seem trying to please the people above them as if they owned them and by scaling the full picture should be close to that. We would be having a pyramid that stretches so narrowly at the top for very few ppl who no one knows and a base that stretches ever so largly so you have a ton of people who work for the law but almost none of them can help.
As I read, 2 line caught my eye. So the first is the policeman's note saying that the court doesn't wait for a crime to be commited it's attracted by the guilt. J.K. didn't commit nothing yet but he was procuted and that's the whole idea. Think about for a second. what would this mean in a real world. What if a tech was developed and allowed the court to guess who's gonna make a crime before the very person even has the smallest thought about the crime comes to his head and there's a hint at that in the beggining suggesting that the higher ups do know who's gonna be guilty eventually. Howver, that's not what Kafka was thinking about. My guess here, he thought that for the court to remain in power the court has to do some work to assert it's role. Therefore, the court cannot wait for someone to commit a crime to start working it must have a reason to work every day 24/7/365. Thus, using the capitalist mind set, if a need is scarce we have to create the need. As I said earlier, they were creating jobs from thin air simply to give people a reason to be there. As a result, what if Joseph wasn't gonna do anything? He was living normally but the court decieded he was gonna be the filling for their work schedule. Meaning J.K. was selected arbitraly and the whole proceeding was meant to break him down until he himself believes he is guilty.
The 2nd line is from the chaplin, when he told the story about the man in the door of justice and how the man was stopped by the guard indefnitly, when the guard explained where the man failed to enter saying that the man believed the guard has power over him. In fact, we see this in the story. At the beggining, J.K. was more confident, stronger and more defiant as the trial went on he got weaker as he accepted the court's authority over him.

title: How  Much Land Does a Man Need
author: Leo Tolstoy
Comments:
A story a bout a farmer Bahom who tried to aquire more and more land Thinking that all his problems were due to the lack of land. One day, to aquire mor land he had to finish a challenge where all he had to do was to circle in 1 day All the land he wants and the land shall be his only if he managed to return to the point where he started otherwise he'd lose the money. title: Le Petit Prince
author: Antoine De Saint Exupery
Comments:
This on was fun in a way I did not expect. I really liked how this book tackeled how we evolve from childhood to aduthood not Necessarily in good way. While the former is known for it's magical sense, the book uses this to it's advantage. We see le Petit Prince, a fever dream like character, is perfect to see the gap between childhood and adulthood. (It't been years since I read it so I lost some of the plot and charactrs but I remember that we had some emphasis on the gap between the mind of a child and that of an adult which we can see in the dialog with the Geograph.)
I enjoyed how the book was kid like with adult depth. I feel like the author was trying to show us the magic we lose as we grow up, the magic of wonder and the simplicity of thinking like a child.

Reread: 31-05-2026 - 01-06-2026
So the little prince visited a king, a conciesed man (The Narcist), a tippler (The drunken man), a businessman, a lamplighter, a geographe and then he visited earh.
Then on earth we meet the snake, the fox, a merchant and a train track switcher.
I again must say this book is written for adults in the language of children. Each character is a diffrent metaphor of certain contradictions.
The king is a metaphor for authority, the conciesed man is about ego and so on.
I like how Easy it is to pick up and understand the themes of this book. This book uses the logic of kids to break the paradox we set ourselves in, we see this in the Geograph, the busniss man and even the tippler. I believe this deeply, the happiest state of men is his kid state. At that state lies are meaningless, we only seek truth and we are free from the systems that traps our logic in circles. the circle is seen in the lamp lighter which image is deeply poetic: He keeps following the order despite the order becoming Obsolete and practically no longer doable. His tragedy however, lies in the fact his ignorant or unintrested to the beauty of what he does. Simply a gear in a machine.
In the house of the dead I said how we are all children from the inside but life hardens us like the boiling water does to the egg. This author however is lighting another side of that equation. Usually, we think that kids are the ones that require explanations to understand stuff. However, the 1st chapter declares the very opposite suggesting that Adults are the ones who require many explanation to see the picture. this made me look at it as if each is living on a seprate world or spectrum. The book is highliting one key diffrence. "Le petit Prince ne renonce jamais a une question une fois qu'il la pose.". His curiosity has no bounderies and he never gave up on understanding what he sees. One thing too that always catches me off guard is how the little prince is able to manafest his will in the world like that's the natural way of things. Like he simply looks at fox and starts talking to him. A snake is his friend and so on.
However, about the ending, I have a gut feeling about it. I think the little prince really died after the snake bit him. I think the more and more the prince was frequenting the world of the adults the more he was getting sick of that world and the more he lost his magical vision about the world and so after a year on earth he could no longer travel back and he was sickened by that world that he had enough.
Or could be just me! Who knows? HeHe ;)

The book I wrote: tho I inspired it from the Alchimist as you may see the similarities from here and there you can also tell that I had diffrent answer to deliver... The irony is this was written as a self help for myself.

Well the story, is simple enough you got a guy lost in the mniddle of nowhere in a foggy desert. I mean how deep can this be? right? How many projections can you fit in there

SPOILER ALERT:
So following up my comment on this being a self help it was due to the facy that at the moment where I started writing I had to face the idea of uncertainty wether my efforts towards a certain goal will ever be enough. Well in a simulated you can bang your head over over again and again until you figure things out life doesn't give you such luxury and you have to pretty much guess where you land with every step you get hence the fog. While the journey goal is self explantory and easily projected on reality there are a couple more projections to consider. The silent desert is the lack of answers during the trial there's mostly nothing to refer to to find your way as you venture your way into life as it's everyone's 1st time; there + Nothing that works for others would certainly work for you for the simple reason of the diffrent cirmstances give birth to diffrent questions that require diffrent answers. Next if you consider the sun as a projection it would most certainly the how the life of the other would look to your eye.
Most people even if unitentionnly would hide their vulnrability and doubts meaning in essence they look like they figured everything out fitting their role neatly. Just like the sun looks at the fog walker.
Last we have our main cast to look upon. The fog walker is basically me... not exactly... So in a way he's a mix of what I am and I want to be. So the role of the fog walker was to stress test my stocism. Complex words?
in essence, the fog walker's job was in a way to see how far the idea that giving up and cracking under the pressure is the worst choice I can make. easy enough right? not exactly. The idea was for him to be the armor of test. However, as Icontrolled his action it wasn't emotions and stamina that was challenged but rather his own philosophy hence the introduction of the man in white a voice that I automatically shut by the voice of whom I need to be to carry on further.
This should allow the proper framing for the plot and the ending. If you didn' like it I appologize but no other ending will give you any satisfaction as that's the only possible true ending and I beg to think of an ending where he leaves the fog and finally makes out of the desert. he would be as much dead to you as he is now to you. Additionally, you know his pursuit for greatness per his definition is eternal thus the only ending is the one I gave him and he'll loop back to another mad trial over and over till he no longer can. Besides the purpose of my writing was the challengem and the peak of challenges for his philosophy is death itself which will project back to me in a failure I couldn't recover from.
